exposure: Absence of routine supplemental oxygen administration post-cesarean
outcome: Frequency of supplemental oxygen administration required
cohort: The study included 324 healthy, term, low-risk parturients undergoing cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.
finding: The incidence of postoperative oxygen desaturation in healthy parturients undergoing elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia was uncommon (0.3%), suggesting routine administration of supplemental oxygen in the PACU is unnecessary.
mod_finding: For healthy parturients undergoing elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia, routine administration of supplemental oxygen in the PACU is unnecessary due to a very low incidence of postoperative oxygen desaturation.
followup_time: N/A (monitoring occurred continuously in the PACU immediately after delivery)
cross-section timing: Continuous monitoring in the Postanesthesia Care Unit (PACU) immediately after cesarean delivery.
